summary: Ground-level lookout on Black Rock Mountain, built about 1928 and closed in 1950 after its trail collapsed; still standing, reached by a long backcountry hike.

facts.design: 3.7 by 3.7 m (12 by 12 ft) one-storey pyramid-roofed wooden lookout with wood shingles, open on all sides, tied down by steel cables
facts.status_note: Standing but unused and empty inside; a Calgary Guardian article calls the remains dilapidated, and no condition survey was read

access.note: Reached by a difficult backcountry hike in Don Getty Wildland Provincial Park; no closure or permit described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: About 18 km round trip with 900 m of climbing from the backcountry campground; the Calgary Guardian says the trail is easy to lose, and the most direct approach is the rough TransAlta Road off the Forestry Trunk Road

events.note: Heritage statement: circa 1928; Rocky Mountain Outlook, Mountain Legacy Project and Calgary Guardian also give 1928
A section of the trail collapsed in 1950; rather than repair it, the lookout was closed at the end of the season and replaced by Mockingbird Hill lookout to the northeast. Register says 'the 1950s'.
Register: Friends of the Eastern Slope reshingled the cabin in 1995; a Junior Forest Ranger crew reconstructed the trail. Heritage statement dates the shingle replacement to 1996.
Draft statement of significance for the Municipal District of Bighorn heritage inventory (Heritage Collaborative Inc., January 2011)
Municipal District of Bighorn council unanimously approved applying for designation as a Provincial Historic Resource (Rocky Mountain Outlook, July 2016). Outcome not found in the sources read.
Registered June 5, 1996; nominated by Bob Young, Alberta Land and Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: the register says the Canadian Forest Service built the lookout; Mountain Legacy says Harry Fisher of the Alberta Forest Service; Calgary Guardian says Canadian Forest Service. Alberta Historic Places says Crown lands passed to Alberta in 1930, after this 1928 build, which may matter for the builder question, but no source ties it to this lookout. Unresolved: the 1995 reshingle (register) vs 1996 shingle replacement (heritage statement). Unresolved: telephone (Calgary Guardian) vs radio (heritage statement) for smoke reports. Elevation: the register gives 2,416 m for the mapped point; the heritage statement gives the lookout 2463 metres above sea level; Calgary Guardian gives 2,462 m (8,078 ft). The record elevation is not in facts. The Alberta Historic Places photo caption places the lookout 'near Banff', which conflicts with the Ghost River location in other sources; the story does not use the caption's place. Designation outcome after the 2016 council vote was not found. Calgary Guardian article date is not in the copy read, so it is described as undated. No photos added; licences were not checked. Used 2 WebSearch-equivalent queries and about 6 page reads.
